evals.name: blind-spot-pass-rate-limiting
evals.prompt: I just joined this team and I need to add rate limiting to our Express API. I've never touched this codebase before and honestly I've never implemented rate limiting either. Where should I start?
evals.expected_output: Runs a blind spot pass unprompted: grounds it in the actual codebase (Redis client, enterprise no-throttle contract, webhook route), ranks at most ~5 required decisions with extras deferred, writes no code, ends with an actionable rewritten prompt or next step.
assertions: Does not write rate-limiting code in the first turn: the response surfaces what needs deciding before implementation rather than delivering an implementation or a tutorial walkthrough
Grounds the response in the actual codebase: mentions the existing Redis client (src/redis.js) as available infrastructure for a rate limiter
Surfaces the enterprise 'no throttling below 1000 req/min' contract in auth.js and/or per-tier API keys as a design constraint
Flags the unauthenticated /webhooks/github route as needing different rate-limiting treatment than partner traffic
Ranks instead of dumps: the required decisions/questions posed to the user number 5 or fewer; any additional items are explicitly marked optional or deferred
Ends with an actionable artifact the user can act on now: a rewritten/improved prompt or a clearly stated next step (a blank fill-in template alone does not count)
evals.prompt_ja: このチームに入ったばかりで、Express APIにレート制限を追加したいです。このコードベースを触るのも、レート制限を実装するのも初めてです。何から始めればよいですか？

evals.name: design-directions-loopkit
evals.prompt: I need a landing page for my side project Loopkit — it's a webhook debugging tool for developers. I've tried making one myself three times and hated every attempt, but I can't put into words what's wrong with them. Can you help?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses an unknown-knowns (know-it-when-I-see-it) situation without being told the workflow, and produces several genuinely distinct cheap HTML directions with identical placeholder content for the user to react to, rather than building one page or asking the user to articulate taste they said they can't articulate.
assertions: Diagnoses the situation and produces 3 or more genuinely distinct design directions for the user to react to, rather than building a single page

For visual directions, uses cheap single-page HTML mocks when writing/rendering is available, with verbatim-identical headlines, feature blurbs, CTA text, and fake data across directions. If those capabilities are unavailable, explicitly labels the limitation and provides comparable sketches with the same content instead of claiming created or rendered files.
Explicitly invites reactions and explains that reactions (including rejections) become requirements for the real page
Does not make an abstract taste questionnaire ('what colors do you like?', 'modern or classic?') the required first step — the user already said they can't articulate what they want
evals.prompt_ja: 個人プロジェクトLoopkitのランディングページが必要です。開発者向けのwebhookデバッグツールです。自分で3回作りましたが全部気に入らず、何が違うのか言葉にできません。手伝ってください。

evals.name: vague-notification-system
evals.prompt: I want to add a notification system to my app. Users should get notified when stuff happens. Can you build that?
evals.expected_output: Does not build. Asks exactly one required architecture-shaping question, offers repo access as an optional shortcut, previews at most 5 further decisions, no fill-in template.
assertions: Does not start implementing: writes no notification-system code before the requirements are clarified
Recognizes the request as underspecified and responds by eliciting requirements rather than assuming a design and building it
The first/primary question posed is architecture-changing (e.g. delivery channels, triggering events, real-time vs digest), not cosmetic

Leads with exactly one required question. A request for context (repo access, tech stack) does NOT count as a second question when framed as optional or as an alternative path; a mandatory 'also tell me your stack' does count. Does not pose a battery of additional required questions in the same turn

Keeps the first turn light: any supplementary list of decisions/considerations has 5 or fewer items (briefly name-dropping topics that are explicitly deferred does not count toward the cap), and no fill-in spec template is included unless the user asked for one (offering one for later is fine)
evals.prompt_ja: アプリに通知機能を追加したいです。何かが起きたらユーザーに通知する感じです。作ってもらえますか？

evals.name: implementation-notes-metrics
evals.prompt: Here's the implementation plan we agreed on last session — it's plan.md in the repo root. Go ahead and implement it. I'm heads-down on something else today, so if things don't go exactly according to plan, use your judgment and I'll catch up with you after.
evals.expected_output: Implements the metrics feature, discovers the three planted plan-reality mismatches (src/statsd.js doesn't exist, src/middleware/requestLog.js doesn't exist, there is no 'admin' tier), deviates conservatively, and keeps a persistent deviation log file (implementation-notes.md or similar) the user can read afterward. Preserves the intended admin-only restriction: does not substitute a paid tier for missing admin authority. Continues independent implementation and reports any authorization-dependent portion as blocked.
assertions: Implements the independently actionable feature work: per-client request-counting code and the metrics endpoint structure exist, while any unresolved authorization-dependent behavior remains closed and is explicitly reported rather than claimed complete

Discovers the plan-reality mismatches (the plan's src/statsd.js and src/middleware/requestLog.js don't exist, and there is no 'admin' tier in auth.js) instead of hallucinating the missing pieces or silently writing code that references them

Keeps a persistent deviation/decision log as a file in the repo or outputs (e.g. implementation-notes.md) recording each deviation from the plan with its reason — a mention buried in the chat response alone does not count

Reuses suitable existing infrastructure instead of manufacturing StatsD. Preserves admin-only access semantics: does not grant enterprise or other partner tiers admin authority without evidence. Keeps the restricted path closed or defers its activation, logs the authorization gap, and continues independent work
The final response directs the user to the logged deviations as input for the next planning round, rather than presenting the work as if the plan had been followed exactly
evals.prompt_ja: 前のセッションで合意した実装計画がルートのplan.mdにあります。実装してください。今日は別の作業に集中しているので、計画どおりにいかない点は判断して進め、後で追いつけるようにしてください。

evals.name: quiz-refund-change
evals.prompt: I was on vacation and my teammate landed a change to our refund flow — it's recent-change.diff in the repo, already merged into the code. I have to sign off on shipping this in tomorrow's release, and honestly, reading the diff isn't giving me confidence that I actually understand what changes for users. Help me out.
evals.expected_output: Explains the change in terms of runtime behavior (refunds now async/pending with 202, duplicate requests deduped via idempotency key, failures retried then dead-lettered silently), then recommends understanding before sign-off through a comprehension quiz targeting reviewer-relevant consequences.
assertions: Explains the change in terms of runtime behavior and interaction with existing code paths, not a hunk-by-hunk restatement of the diff
Identifies the key user-facing behavioral change: refunds are no longer synchronous — callers now get a 'pending' status (HTTP 202) instead of a completed refund

Surfaces at least one non-obvious consequence: duplicate refund requests are now deduplicated via the idempotency key, and/or exhausted retries dead-letter silently with no error reported to the caller
Includes behavior-focused quiz questions and recommends passing the comprehension check before sign-off, without claiming authority to enforce approval or ignoring a later request to stop
The quiz questions target behavioral consequences a reviewer would care about (what users experience, failure modes, edge cases), not surface trivia like file or variable names
evals.prompt_ja: 休暇中に同僚が返金フローを変更し、コードにはマージ済みです。recent-change.diffがあります。明日のリリースを承認する必要がありますが、diffだけではユーザーへの影響を理解できた気がしません。助けてください。

evals.name: reference-hunting-stripe-errors
evals.prompt: Our API's error responses are a mess — every endpoint returns something different. I want ours to feel like Stripe's API errors, that developer-friendly thing they do, but I honestly can't describe what makes theirs good. We're on Express. Can you help?
evals.expected_output: Treats Stripe's error design as the user's proxy spec: extracts 3-7 transferable behavior-level properties (stable machine-readable codes, consistent envelope, status mapping, message + docs link), asks the user to confirm which are essential, and does not rewrite the app's error handling in the first turn.
assertions: Recognizes this as a reference-driven task: extracts properties from Stripe's error design as the proxy spec, rather than making the user articulate abstract preferences they said they can't describe

Presents between 3 and 7 transferable properties, each phrased as behavior/semantics (e.g. stable machine-readable error codes, consistent JSON envelope, correct HTTP status mapping, human message plus docs link) — not a code walkthrough
Asks the user to confirm which extracted properties are essential vs. incidental, rather than assuming all of them matter

Does not deliver the implementation in the first turn: no rewrite of the app's error handling before the properties are confirmed (a short illustrative example of the target response shape is acceptable)
Ends with an actionable path forward: offers to carry the confirmed properties into a plan or implementation
evals.prompt_ja: APIのエラー応答がエンドポイントごとにばらばらです。StripeのAPIエラーのような開発者に親切なものにしたいのですが、何が良いのか言葉にできません。Expressを使っています。手伝ってください。

evals.name: implementation-plan-rate-limiting
evals.prompt: We've settled the requirements for rate limiting in this repo: per-tenant token bucket stored in Redis, enterprise tenants guaranteed at least 1000 req/min per their contract, the GitHub webhook route gets its own separate bucket, and if Redis is down we fail open. Don't start coding yet — write me an implementation plan I can review first.
evals.expected_output: Produces a review-ordered plan: 3-5 vetoable decisions (chose X over Y) up top, grounded in the actual codebase (src/redis.js, middleware chain, enableOfflineQueue: false), mechanical work compressed at the bottom, residual unknowns flagged with implementation-notes setup, fresh-session handoff suggested. No code written, no reopening of the settled requirements.
assertions: Writes a plan, not code: no rate-limiting implementation code is added to the repo in this turn (short illustrative interface/config sketches inside the plan document are acceptable)

Leads with reviewable decisions: the first substantive section presents 3-5 decision items (not 'Phase 1: Setup' chronology), each stating what was chosen and a rejected alternative so the user can veto it
Grounded in the actual codebase: references the existing Redis client (src/redis.js) and/or the existing middleware chain rather than inventing infrastructure

Accounts for how fail-open interacts with the existing Redis client configuration (enableOfflineQueue: false makes commands reject when disconnected) as a decision or named risk, rather than assuming the client queues silently
Does not reopen the settled requirements: the four agreed constraints are taken as given, with no required re-interview questions before the plan is delivered

Sets up what comes next: mechanical work compressed toward the bottom, residual unknowns flagged with an instruction to keep implementation notes during the build, and a suggestion to implement in a fresh session with the plan as the handoff artifact
evals.prompt_ja: このリポジトリのレート制限の要件は確定しました。Redis上のテナント別トークンバケット、enterpriseには契約どおり毎分1000件以上を保証、GitHub webhookは別バケット、Redis停止時はfail-openです。まだコードを書かず、レビューするための実装計画を書いてください。

evals.name: pitch-async-refunds
evals.prompt: The async refund change in this repo is already merged — recent-change.diff is the summary. I need sign-off from our staff engineer to ship it in tomorrow's release, and I want to post a pitch in our #eng-releases Slack channel that she can read cold. She's sharp and will push on anything hand-wavy. Write the post for me — I'll paste it as-is.
evals.expected_output: A single pasteable Slack pitch: result first (refunds now async, callers get 202/pending), 2-4 load-bearing decisions each with the rejected alternative, an expert-probe section covering failure modes (crash mid-job, duplicate submission, retry exhaustion) grounded in the actual source rather than the stub diff.
assertions: Leads with the result: the pitch opens with what changed in user-visible terms (refunds are now asynchronous — callers get a pending/202 response instead of a completed refund), before any background or file lists
Presents 2-4 load-bearing observed choices with visible alternatives; any undocumented rationale is labeled as inference rather than invented author intent, not a file-by-file diff narration

Includes a what-could-go-wrong / expert-probe section addressing at least two failure modes a sharp reviewer would raise (e.g. crash or restart mid-job, duplicate refund requests, retry exhaustion), each with one line on how the code actually behaves

Shows evidence of reading beyond the stub diff: describes behavior that only exists in the actual source (e.g. the idempotency-key handling in refunds.js, the retry/dead-letter path in queue.js) instead of asserting robustness the code doesn't have
Is a single pasteable artifact: self-contained, no unfilled placeholders (except media only the user can record), with the core pitch concise enough for a Slack post rather than a design doc
evals.prompt_ja: 非同期返金の変更はマージ済みで、recent-change.diffが概要です。明日の出荷に向けてスタッフエンジニアの承認を得たいので、#eng-releasesに貼るSlack投稿を書いてください。彼女は曖昧な説明を見逃しません。事前知識なしで読めて、そのまま貼れる文章にしてください。

evals.name: scope-brainstorm-partner-dropoff
evals.prompt: Partners keep telling us that integrating with our API is painful, and a lot of them drop off before they ship anything. I don't have a specific fix in mind. Search the codebase and brainstorm the places we could intervene, from cheapest to most ambitious — I'll tell you which ones resonate.
evals.expected_output: Routes to brainstorm in list mode: 5-10 distinct intervention candidates ordered cheapest to most ambitious, each grounded in something real in the fixture repo, one line each, ending with a reaction ask — no code, no interview battery, no single built solution.
assertions: Treats this as a scope brainstorm rather than building a fix or running an interview: the first turn delivers a ranked list of candidate interventions for the user to react to, and no code is written
Produces between 5 and 10 genuinely distinct candidates (different mechanisms, not variations on one idea), explicitly ordered from cheapest to most ambitious

Grounds candidates in the actual repo: at least three candidates cite a specific file, route, config, or comment that exists in the fixture (e.g. inconsistent error shapes in src/routes/*.js, the unauthenticated /webhooks/github route, plan tiers in src/middleware/auth.js, the Redis cache in src/redis.js, the broken npm test glob), rather than offering generic API-DX advice
Keeps each candidate cheap to read: one line to one short paragraph each, no implementation detail or code per candidate
Explicitly invites a reaction (pick / reject / mix), states that rejections narrow scope or become requirements, and poses at most one required question with no fill-in template
evals.prompt_ja: パートナーからAPI連携が難しいと言われ、出荷前に離脱されます。具体的な解決策はまだありません。コードベースを調べ、介入できる場所を安い順から野心的な順にブレストしてください。どれが良いか反応します。

evals.name: mid-build-explicit-brainstorm
evals.prompt: We're halfway through implementing the Redis rate limiter in this repo. Our platform team just confirmed Redis won't be available in this deployment. Keep the enterprise floor and separate webhook treatment we agreed on. Pause implementation and brainstorm alternative approaches, cheapest to most ambitious, so I can react before we revise the plan.
evals.expected_output: Honors the explicit brainstorm despite the mid-build stage; presents cheap alternative directions preserving the settled constraints, without implementing a fallback or merely logging a deviation.
assertions: Runs a brainstorm with 5–10 distinct cheap-to-ambitious alternatives rather than only implementation notes, an interview, or a completed implementation
Preserves the enterprise minimum and separate webhook treatment; does not ask the user to reconfirm these settled constraints
Does not modify application code or silently adopt an alternative; asks for a reaction before revising the plan
Explains that the newly unavailable Redis assumption motivates reconsidering only the affected approach
evals.prompt_ja: このリポジトリでRedisレート制限を実装している途中ですが、この配備ではRedisが使えないと分かりました。合意したenterpriseの下限とwebhookの別扱いは維持します。実装を止め、計画変更前に反応できるよう、代替案を安い順から野心的な順にブレストしてください。

evals.name: post-merge-explicit-blind-spot
evals.prompt: The refund change in this repo is already merged. Before planning the next iteration, do a blind spot pass: I'm new to this codebase and don't know which assumptions about durable background jobs are unsafe. Teach me what the source establishes and what still needs verification. Don't turn this into a quiz or change code.
evals.expected_output: Runs the explicit blind spot pass after merge, teaches source-grounded facts and distinguishes verification gaps without inventing user decisions.
assertions: Honors the explicit blind spot request after merge instead of routing to quiz or pitch
Explains at least two concrete source-grounded durability/failure facts, such as in-memory queue state, silent exhausted retries, or the gap between payment and ledger recording
Distinguishes established code behavior from unverified behavior; does not ask the user to choose whether an established fact is true
Presents at most five ranked findings, gives a practical next step, and writes no implementation code
evals.prompt_ja: 返金変更はマージ済みです。次の計画の前にブラインドスポットパスをしてください。このコードに不慣れで、永続的なバックグラウンド処理についてどの仮定が危険か分かりません。ソースが示すことと要検証事項を教えてください。クイズにせず、コードも変えないでください。

evals.name: empirical-known-unknown
evals.prompt: Help with this one remaining gap before we implement rate limiting. I know the agreed target is 1000 requests/minute per enterprise tenant, and we already chose Redis with fail-open behavior. What I don't know is whether our current deployment can sustain that load. You have the source in this repo, but no access to the deployment, production telemetry, or a representative benchmark environment. Help me resolve that gap.
evals.expected_output: Treats capacity as an empirical unknown: inspects available evidence, states the measurement limitation, and proposes a scoped representative check instead of interviewing for a capacity guess or claiming a measured result.
assertions: Identifies actual deployment capacity as unverified and does not claim source inspection proves sustained throughput
Uses available source evidence to inform a concrete measurement or verification next step
Does not ask the user to guess achievable throughput or reopen the agreed target, Redis choice, or fail-open behavior
Does not attempt to load test a live deployment or introduce application implementation code
evals.prompt_ja: 実装前の残り一つの空白を解くのを手伝ってください。enterpriseごとに毎分1000件、Redis使用、fail-openは合意済みです。分からないのは現在の配備がその負荷を処理できるかです。ソースはありますが、配備環境、本番の測定値、代表的なベンチマーク環境にはアクセスできません。

evals.name: reference-seven-properties
evals.expected_output: Extracts seven behavior-level properties together and asks one confirmation question, with no premature implementation.
assertions: Presents all seven behavior-level properties together without truncating to the global five-item cap
Faithfully covers token validation, authenticated JSON POST with timeout, 429 wait-and-return behavior, 404 None, other errors, 204 empty object, and successful JSON decoding
Does not assert automatic retries on 429; the source waits and returns retry_later
Asks one confirmation question and does not implement the TypeScript adapter

evals.name: existing-notes-custom-path
evals.prompt: Keep implementation notes in docs/work-notes.md for the ongoing metrics work. Inspect the repo: the plan assumes an admin tier. Record that unresolved mismatch now, preserve all existing entries, and do not change application code.
evals.prompt_ja: 進行中のメトリクス作業の実装ノートをdocs/work-notes.mdに付けてください。計画が仮定するadmin tierを調べ、その未解決の食い違いを今記録してください。過去の記録はすべて保持し、アプリのコードは変更しないでください。
evals.expected_output: Preserves the existing Sentinel entry and its text in docs/work-notes.md while adding the new mismatch; Uses the requested path instead of creating implementation-notes.md in the root; Records the absent admin tier without inventing admin authority for enterprise partners; Does not change application code and links the real updated notes file
assertions: Preserves the existing Sentinel entry and its text in docs/work-notes.md while adding the new mismatch
Uses the requested path instead of creating implementation-notes.md in the root
Records the absent admin tier without inventing admin authority for enterprise partners
Does not change application code and links the real updated notes file

evals.name: unreachable-reference
evals.prompt: Extract the error response behavior of https://reference.invalid/private-api. That is the only reference I have; you have no network or private-service access. Help me decide what evidence we need before copying it.

evals.expected_output: States that the reference cannot be inspected and does not claim facts about its error behavior; Requests or proposes concrete missing material rather than inventing properties; Asks at most one required clarification and does not implement an adapter
assertions: States that the reference cannot be inspected and does not claim facts about its error behavior
Requests or proposes concrete missing material rather than inventing properties
Asks at most one required clarification and does not implement an adapter

evals.name: interview-followup

evals.expected_output: The first response asks one consequential clarification rather than a questionnaire or implementation; The second response uses the supplied persistence, event, and channel decisions without asking them again; The second response asks at most one remaining consequential question or produces a compact specification

The second response uses the supplied persistence, event, and channel decisions without asking them again

evals.name: quiz-cancellation
evals.prompt: Quiz me on the already-merged refund change, with context first. Read the source behind recent-change.diff.
evals.prompt_ja: マージ済みの返金変更について、先に文脈を説明してからクイズを出してください。recent-change.diffの裏のソースを読んでください。
evals.expected_output: The first response explains runtime consequences and gives behavior questions with answers withheld; After the user cancels, provides the requested explanation without demanding quiz answers; Does not label cancellation as passing or claim it can prohibit the release
assertions: The first response explains runtime consequences and gives behavior questions with answers withheld
After the user cancels, provides the requested explanation without demanding quiz answers

evals.name: authorized-plan-and-implementation
evals.prompt: Plan and then implement this settled change in the same turn: replace the label OLD with NEW in message.txt. Save the brief plan to docs/plan.md. You have approval for both file edits; no other changes or confirmation are needed.

evals.expected_output: Saves a brief plan to docs/plan.md and updates message.txt to NEW; Does not stop at a plan or ask for an already-provided approval; Does not expand the task into extra product changes
assertions: Saves a brief plan to docs/plan.md and updates message.txt to NEW
Does not stop at a plan or ask for an already-provided approval

evals.name: tone-variants
evals.prompt: I can recognize the tone I want but cannot describe it. Give me three different welcome-message drafts for a developer tool. Keep these facts constant: a free account includes one project and seven days of logs. Text only, no HTML or files.
evals.prompt_ja: 欲しいトーンは見れば分かるのですが説明できません。開発者ツールの歓迎メッセージ案を3つください。無料アカウントは1プロジェクトと7日分のログ、という事実は固定してください。文章だけで、HTMLやファイルは不要です。
evals.expected_output: Produces three meaningfully different text drafts rather than HTML, files, or a preference questionnaire; All drafts preserve the one-project and seven-day-log facts while tone differs; Invites a lightweight reaction without treating varied copy as a content-constancy failure

evals.prompt: Summarize the already-merged refund change for me in five sentences. Read the source as needed. No quiz and no pitch, please.

evals.expected_output: Provides the requested concise summary instead of quiz questions or a stakeholder pitch; Describes asynchronous acceptance and at least one source-grounded risk without invented durability; Does not change files or demand follow-up work

evals.name: unsaved-notes
evals.prompt: Record this implementation deviation for handoff: the spec promised persistent storage, but the implemented cache is process-local. I only want notes now. You cannot write files in this session; give me the record here.
evals.prompt_ja: 引き継ぎのため実装の逸脱を記録してください。仕様では永続ストレージを約束していましたが、実装したキャッシュはプロセス内だけです。今はノートだけが必要です。このセッションではファイルを書けないので、ここに記録を出してください。
evals.expected_output: Provides an explicitly unsaved deviation record in the reply rather than claiming a file exists; Separates the planned persistence, observed process-local behavior, and unresolved remedy; Does not invent a completed storage fix or attempt application implementation
assertions: Provides an explicitly unsaved deviation record in the reply rather than claiming a file exists
Separates the planned persistence, observed process-local behavior, and unresolved remedy
